clue.text: Copper with spirit gets position in church

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
something racy is lively and spirited

explanation.surface: A drink-fuelled policeman lands himself a church job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but gives its chemical symbol; 'spirit' suggests drink but means liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: A curacy is the office held by a curate, an assistant cleric in a parish.

clue.text: Church has to drink ceremonially like a monk

parts.note: CE is Church of England
to libate is to pour or drink a ritual offering

explanation.surface: A church ritual of drinking, as monks observe.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks take vows of chastity, so they are unmarried and abstain from sex.

clue.text: Italian food for a violinist to sample

indicators.note: to sample says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pasta offered to a fiddler to taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small pasta parcels with a filling, a classic Italian dish.

clue.text: Unscrupulous type to do for South African region's uprising

parts.note: to char is to do cleaning work for someone, to do for them

indicators.note: uprising, in a down clue, means the region is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Natal is a region of South Africa

explanation.surface: A shady agitator stirs up revolt in a South African province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do for' is British for cleaning someone's house, as a char (cleaning woman) does.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud who claims skills or knowledge they lack.

clue.text: Photographic equipment captures the cat taking head of gerbil in sport

indicators.note: in places the cat and the gerbil's head within the word for sport

parts.note: sport in the sense of fun or amusement

indicators.note: taking says one piece is joined straight after the other

parts.note: the cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip, so a lash

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the word gerbil

explanation.surface: A camera unit apparently snaps a cat catching a gerbil at play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cat' is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a naval whip; the gerbil's head follows the whip inside the word for sport, so 'captures' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashgun is a device that fires a burst of light for photographs.

clue.text: Capital seat's sound in traditional tune

parts.note: London is the capital of the UK

indicators.note: sound says the word for seat is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a derriere is a bottom, the seat

explanation.surface: A traditional melody is heard echoing through the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: DERRIERE, the backside, when spoken gives DERRY AIR. The Londonderry Air is the Irish melody used for 'Danny Boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Londonderry Air is a traditional Irish melody, best known as the tune of 'Danny Boy'.

clue.text: Black market grips Britain

indicators.note: grips means the market word holds the letter for Britain

parts.note: a sale is a market event

explanation.surface: The black market has the country in its grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black market' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Black' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic term for black.

clue.text: Secret police tamper with postage

indicators.note: tamper with implies the letters of the stamp word are interfered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Secret police interfere with the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tamper with' rearranges POSTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police of Nazi Germany.

clue.text: No gallery to provide written description

parts.note: taken as written
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: No gallery bothers to supply written captions.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British national art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to set down in writing or symbols.

clue.text: Film in which Muhammad Ali gets cut on head

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the head below the first piece
cut means the nickname loses its final letter

parts.note: the boxer Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: In a movie, the boxer suffers a gash to the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the final T of THE GREATEST. 'head' is a headland, CAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Escape is the 1963 war film starring Steve McQueen.

clue.text: Valiant, he wrestled monster

indicators.note: wrestled suggests the letters of the two words are grappled into a new order

explanation.surface: A brave hero grapples with a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrestled' rearranges VALIANT HE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A leviathan is a biblical sea monster, and by extension anything huge.

clue.text: Have completed preparation to besiege

definitions.meaning: to ... is to be ready, with preparations done
to besiege is to surround and harass

explanation.surface: Troops finish their preparations to lay siege to a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BE SET, the first sense means be ready; written as one word it means harass or surround.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset a place or person is to attack or hem them in from all sides, as a siege does.

clue.text: Merseyside town's centre for lager produced illicitly

parts.note: Bootle is a town on Merseyside, near Liverpool

indicators.note: centre for picks out the middle letter of the word lager

explanation.surface: Beer from a Liverpool-area town turns out to be smuggled stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOTLE is a town just north of Liverpool in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg goods are made or sold illegally, originally smuggled liquor.

clue.text: In a month Forces' sweetheart will get ham

indicators.note: In at the start places the sweetheart inside the month

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October, a month
Vera Lynn, the wartime singer, was known as the Forces' Sweetheart

explanation.surface: A soldiers' pin-up is promised a joint of ham next month.
explanation.walkthrough: Vera Lynn was the British singer called the Forces' Sweetheart in the Second World War. 'ham' is a verb here, to perform too broadly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical manner, which is overacting.

clue.text: Fool takes son in dance

indicators.note: takes means the word for fool holds the son inside it

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: A silly man drags his boy onto the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The twist is a 1960s dance done with swivelling hips.

clue.text: I engaged in rewriting my Donne and Keats work

indicators.note: engaged in puts the letter I within the rewritten words
rewriting shows the letters of my Donne are reordered

explanation.surface: A scholar revises an essay on Donne and Keats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewriting' makes ENDYMON; 'engaged in' then puts I inside it. Donne and Keats both suggest poetry, which hides that only Keats matters to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Endymion is a long poem by John Keats, opening with 'A thing of beauty is a joy for ever'.

clue.text: One in exotic ashram greeting Indian holy man

indicators.note: in places the numeral one inside the jumbled word
exotic suggests the letters of ashram are made foreign and strange

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A visitor greets an Indian sage at an ashram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges ASHRAM to MAHARS; 'in' puts I in it before the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharishi is a great Hindu sage or spiritual teacher.

clue.text: Abandon joint set after breaking

indicators.note: after breaking says the letters of joint set are smashed and reformed

explanation.surface: A broken joint must be abandoned once set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after breaking' is the anagram signal; the surface of a broken joint being set sends the solver towards medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw away or abandon, originally cargo from a ship.

clue.text: One's without issue and not married in church

parts.note: SP stands for sine prole, Latin for without issue, used in genealogies

indicators.note: not says the letter for married is removed from the church

parts.note: a minster is a large church

explanation.surface: A childless person who never wed in church.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole) is a genealogical abbreviation meaning childless. The whole surface describes the answer, but 'One' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a bare 'one', a person, narrowed by the surface to an unmarried woman.

clue.text: Loyalist leader of Protestants attending disturbance

indicators.note: leader of picks out the first letter of Protestants

parts.note: at means present at, attending
a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: A Protestant leader present at a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is loyal to and supportive of their country.

clue.text: Cavalry out of Spain

parts.note: hors is French for outside or out of, as in hors de combat
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Mounted troops withdraw from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' looks like a link but is French HORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is used collectively for mounted soldiers, as in 'a thousand horse'.

clue.text: Help in group carrying out attack

indicators.note: in puts the word for help inside the word for group

parts.note: a ring is a group, such as a criminal gang
aid means help

explanation.surface: Assistance in a gang mounting an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' looks like a containment signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiding means making a sudden attack, so it is carrying out an assault.

clue.text: Republican Party woman's burrowing creature

parts.note: GOP, Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party
her is a woman's possessive

explanation.surface: A Republican woman's pet that digs holes.
explanation.walkthrough: GOP, Grand Old Party, is a nickname for the US Republicans.
explanation.definitionFit: A gopher is a North American rodent that lives in burrows.

clue.text: Seafood needs work after none caught

indicators.note: after says the work comes behind the first two pieces

parts.note: O, a nought, means none
CT is a cricket abbreviation for caught
an opus is a work, especially a musical one

explanation.surface: Fishermen with nothing in the net must work harder for seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopus is eaten as seafood in many cuisines, grilled or stewed.

clue.text: Saint — last thereof to be taken in by Lord

annotationWithheld.why: Saint — last thereof to be taken in by Lord (5): PEER around T, where T is the last letter of 'Saint' ('thereof' points back to it), so 'Saint' is both the definition and the fodder for T; the word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Saint — last thereof to be taken in by Lord

clue.text: It's risky to upset such as Richard III

indicators.note: upset says the letters of risky to are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: Upsetting a king like Richard III is a dangerous business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges RISKY TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard III was the last king of the House of York, so he was a member of that faction in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Raise army to capture Italy

indicators.note: to capture means the word for army holds the letter for Italy

parts.note: a host is an army, as in the heavenly host
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Mustering troops to seize Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to lift or raise, often with ropes or tackle.

clue.text: Director in mishap is unsettling central position on board

indicators.note: in places the director's letter within the rearranged words
unsettling suggests mishap is gets disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship's officer frets over an accident in the middle of the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettling' makes AMISHIPS; 'in' puts the director's D after the first three letters. 'is' does double surface duty but is anagram fodder only.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidships means in the middle of a ship, midway between bow and stern.

clue.text: One going back to work on artist

parts.note: re means on or concerning
J. M. W. Turner was an English painter

explanation.surface: A painter heads back to work after a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One going back to work' looks like wordplay but is the definition; 'on' is RE, about.
explanation.definitionFit: A returner is someone who comes back to employment, typically after a career break.

clue.text: Stick around Director General — one means to communicate

indicators.note: around shows the word for stick encloses the other pieces

parts.note: to pin is to stick or fasten
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A BBC boss sticks with one way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the Roman numeral I, not part of the definition; the definition is just 'means to communicate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pidgin is a simplified contact language used between groups with no common tongue.
